ISSUE
Approve First Amendment to Agreement No. A-7679 between the City of Palmdale and
Advantage Mailing, LLC for printing, bundling, and delivery of the Palmdale News,
Activities & Entertainment Magazine.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Approve the First Amendment to Agreement No. A-7679 between the City of
  Palmdale and Advantage Mailing, LLC for printing, bundling, and delivery of the
  Palmdale News, Activities & Entertainment Magazine in the overall contract
  amount not to exceed $420,000 for a term of two years; and,

  2. Authorize the Interim City Manager or designee to execute First Amendment to
  Agreement No. A-7679 with Advantage Mailing, LLC including making minimal
  and/or non-substantive changes.

BACKGROUND
The Palmdale News, Activities & Entertainment Magazine is published quarterly (Winter,
Spring, Summer, Fall) to provide residents and businesses with information on City
news, events, and classes. The magazine is mailed to Palmdale residents located in zip
codes 93550, 93552, and 93591; and is distributed to community stakeholders for use
in their recruitments, distributed at community events and throughout City and
community facilities.
In 2021, in an effort to improve the delivery and distribution of the magazine, the City
released a Request for Proposal (RFP) for the printing, bundling, and delivery services.
At the City Council meeting held on October 20, 2021, the Council approved Agreement

No. A-7679 with vendor Advantage Mailing, LLC, the selected vendor through the RFP
process. Agreement No. A-7679 is for $119,128 and includes an option to extend the

First Amendment to Agreement No. A-7679 will allow Staff to exercise the option to
extend the agreement term for two years, including new services, and increase the
overall contract amount not to exceed $420,000, which constitutes an allocation of
$147,200 for FY 22/23 and $153,100 for FY 23/24.
DISCUSSION
Staff recommends approval of the First Amendment to Agreement No. A-7679 to
continue services with Advantage Mailing, LLC for two years. The services received in
2022 from Advantage for printing, mailing, and bundling the magazine demonstrated
they are an experienced vendor who produces a top-quality product, in a timely fashion,
with the ability and flexibility to make changes if needed up to press time and at a good
value.

FISCAL IMPACT
The contract total amount is not to exceed $420,000; funds have been budgeted in FY
22/23 for $147,200 in account 10117001-722330. Funds for FY 23/24 will be appropriated
during the next budget cycle.

ISSUE
Approve Agreement No. A-8142 with Tripod Investments, LLC and Hafrisco, LLC, an
economic development loan in the amount of $2,750,000 for the acquisition of property
located on the southeast corner of Avenue M and 10th Street West.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Approve Agreement A-8142 with Tripod Investments, LLC and Hafrisco, LLC;

  2. Authorize the Interim City Manager or her designee to prepare and execute all
  necessary documents and to make minimal and/or non-substantive changes, as
  needed; and,

  3. Authorize budget appropriations in the amount of $2,750,000.

BACKGROUND
The Successor Agency to the Community Redevelopment Agency of the City of
Palmdale (Successor Agency) owns approximately 118 acres located at the southeast
corner of Avenue M and 10th Street West (Property). On September 20, 2017, the
Successor Agency entered into Purchase and Sale Agreement A-5896 (PSA) to sell the
Property to build a new development that would create hundreds of new jobs for the
community. The City worked closely with the purchaser to find a Fortune 500 company
that will build over a million square feet of new industrial space to support its operations.

On January 27, 2022, the City approved Site Plan Review 21-005 for this new project.
However, California Department of Fish and Wildlife (CDFW) approval is required before
construction can commence and there is a delay in the issuance of the necessary
environmental permits from CDFW. The Property is currently in escrow and the end user

has indicated that it will not close escrow until all necessary permits, including those
from CDFW, has been secured. Although the Property is currently exempt from the
Surplus Land Act, the disposition of the property needs to be completed by
December 31, 2022. If the disposition of the property is not completed before the end of
the year, then the Property would be subject to additional requirements from the State
and there would be no guarantee that the Property would be conveyed to the end user
as intended in the PSA and related Extension Agreements.

DISCUSSION
To avoid any potential delays in the development of the Property, the City will enter into
a City Loan Agreement with Tripod Investments, LLC and Hafrisco, LLC (Borrower) to
close escrow prior to the December 31, 2022, deadline. Loan terms and conditions
include a 14% interest rate plus a $140,800 loan fee to cover the City’s staff and legal
costs. The Borrower can only use the funds to pay the purchase price of the Property to
the Successor Agency. The maturity date will be six (6) months from the Loan date;
however, the City can extend the term, at its sole discretion. If the term is extended, an
additional loan fee and interest will be charged to the Borrower.

To secure the Loan, a First Deed of Trust listing the City as the beneficiary will be
recorded on the Property. The Deed of Trust shall include covenants burdening the
Property and running with the land binding the Borrower and its successors and assigns
to the performance of all obligations of the Borrower set forth in the Purchase and Sale
Agreement, the Settlement Agreement, and the City Loan Agreement. This includes a
condition for the Borrower to convey the property to the end user once all permits
needed for construction to commence have been secured.

FISCAL IMPACT
The Loan will be for $2,750,000. The City will receive $140,800 loan fee plus $192,498 in
interest. If the City extends the term, an additional loan fee and interest will be collected.

the purposes of the PSA and to carry out the Successor Agency’s duties under applicable statutes

ARTICLE I. SUBJECT OF AGREEMENT

Section 1.01  Purpose of the Agreement

  The purpose of this Agreement is to provide for the City’s assistance in financing the
acquisition of the Property for development pursuant to the PSA and the Settlement Agreement.
The acquisition and development and use of the Property pursuant to this Agreement, and the
fulfillment generally of this Agreement, are in the vital and best interests of the City of Palmdale
and the health, safety, morals, and welfare of its residents, and in accord with the public purposes
of the PSA and the Settlement Agreement and the provisions of applicable federal, state, and local

ISSUE
Adopt Resolution No. CC 2022-120, a Resolution of the City Council of the City of
Palmdale authorizing remote teleconference participation for meetings of the City
Council and/or its subordinate legislative bodies for an additional 30-day period.

RECOMMENDATION
Staff recommends that the City Council:
  1. Approve the resolution to thereby extend, for an additional 30-day period, the
  authority of the City Council, and all related and/or subordinate legislative bodies,
  to participate remotely in properly noticed meetings.

BACKGROUND
Since October 1, 2021 and through January 1, 2024, AB 361 has temporarily amended
the Ralph M. Brown Act (California Government Code § 54950 et seq.) to provide more
flexibility regarding participation in public meetings from a remote location. In layman’s
terms AB 361 allows “zoom” meetings if specified requirements are met.
If the City Council authorizes remote meetings, such initial authorization must expire no
later than 30 days from the initial authorization. The City Council is authorized to
thereafter extend the authorization if it makes one of various specified findings.
AB 361 requires several procedural safeguards to protect public participation during a
remote meeting, key ones of which are summarized as follows:
  1. The public must have the ability to address the legislative body directly and must
  be given information on how to address the legislative body;
  2. The public must be provided with either a call-in or internet-based service option;
  3. The legislative body must stop the meeting if the call-in or internet-based option
  fails;

  4. The legislative body cannot require that public comments be submitted in
  advance (although this option can be provided);
  5. Public speakers cannot be required to pre-register for public comment (except as
  required by an independent call-in or internet platform);
  6. Members of the public must be given a reasonable time to register to provide
  public comment; and
  7. Agencies that provide a timed public comment period shall not close the public
  comment period until that time period has expired.
DISCUSSION
The City Council adopted an initial AB 361 Resolution on June 15, 2022. This resolution
has been extended multiple times. The most recent extension is set to expire on
December 2, 2022. The question before the City Council is whether to extend this
authority for an additional 30-day period. An extension of authority to remotely
participate is allowed if (1) the state of emergency continues, and (2) a resolution with
required findings has been adopted within the last 30 days.
The proposed resolution would be immediately effective and allow members of
legislative bodies to continue to participate remotely for an additional thirty days if the
agenda for the meeting has included the legally required participation noticing. The
resolution would also allow the City Manager (or designee) to opt to not include such
noticing, as there may be instances where it would be impractical, due to staffing
considerations, to allow remote participation in meetings.

DISCUSSION
Asphalt materials are used in the Maintenance Division’s daily operations. These
materials are used for pothole patching, sidewalk ramping, and other pavement
maintenance and repairs on citywide streets.
Additional funds on Purchase Order No. 20230013 are needed for the Musical Road
Project. City Street Maintenance staff completed an overlay on 2,500 feet of east and
westbound lanes along Avenue N between Sierra Highway and 10th Street West using
765 tons of hot mix asphalt. The overlay improved the existing condition of the roadway,
providing a smooth surface in preparation for musical road stamp installation.

FISCAL IMPACT
Sufficient funds for the additional Purchase Order line are budgeted in Musical Road
Project Account S0155158-724525. The blanket Purchase Order amount for Asphalt
Materials for FY 2022-2023 will not exceed $169,000.00.
